\section[beurteilen]{beurteilen — to judge, to assess}

\label{lesson:GE-C340-beurteilen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to bring out, then the German for to set out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: beurteilen}
\textbf{beurteilen} — \textquotedblleft{}to judge, to assess\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Das kann ich nicht beurteilen, ich kenne das Buch nicht.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I cannot judge that; I do not know the book.}
\end{quote}

Inseparable: \emph{er beurteilt, er hat beurteilt}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{beurteilen} is built on \emph{Urteil} \textquotedblleft{}judgement\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Old High German \emph{urteil} and Proto-Germanic \emph{uzdailiją} \textquotedblleft{}a dealing out\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), on the word for \textquotedblleft{}part\textquotedblright{}: a judge deals out to each his part.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{beurteilen}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{beurteilen}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{beurteilen}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for to bring out, then the German for to set out, then say \emph{beurteilen} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does beurteilen mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To judge, to assess\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[einschätzen]{einschätzen — to assess, to estimate}

\label{lesson:GE-C340-einschaetzen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to set out, then the German for to judge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: einschätzen}
\textbf{einschätzen} — \textquotedblleft{}to assess, to estimate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ich habe die Zeit falsch eingeschätzt und bin zu spät gekommen.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I misjudged the time and arrived late.}
\end{quote}

Separable: \emph{sie schätzt ein}, \emph{sie hat eingeschätzt}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{einschätzen} is built on \emph{schätzen} \textquotedblleft{}to value, to estimate\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Middle High German \emph{schetzen} (EtymDB), a verb made from \emph{Schatz} \textquotedblleft{}treasure\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for to set out, then the German for to judge, then say \emph{einschätzen} again

\section[die Einschätzung]{die Einschätzung — the assessment}

\label{lesson:GE-C340-einschaetzung}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to judge, then the German for to assess.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: die Einschätzung}
\textbf{die Einschätzung} — \textquotedblleft{}the assessment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Nach meiner Einschätzung brauchen wir zwei Stunden.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In my assessment we need two hours.}
\end{quote}

Plural: \emph{die Einschätzungen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Einschätzung} is formed from \emph{einschätzen} with \emph{-ung} (EtymDB), and \emph{schätzen} goes back to Middle High German \emph{schetzen} \textquotedblleft{}to value\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[kritisieren]{kritisieren — to criticize}

\label{lesson:GE-C340-kritisieren}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to assess, then the German for the assessment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: kritisieren}
\textbf{kritisieren} — \textquotedblleft{}to criticize\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Die Zeitung kritisiert den Bürgermeister wegen der hohen Preise.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The newspaper criticizes the mayor because of the high prices.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Jemanden für etwas kritisieren}. Perfekt: \emph{hat kritisiert}, with no \emph{ge-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kritisieren} goes with \emph{Kritik}, borrowed from French \emph{critique}, which goes back through Latin \emph{criticus} to Greek \emph{kritikós} \textquotedblleft{}able to judge\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kritisieren}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for to assess, then the German for the assessment, then say \emph{kritisieren} again

\section[die Kritik]{die Kritik — the criticism; the review}

\label{lesson:GE-C340-kritik}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for the assessment, then the German for to criticize.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: die Kritik}
\textbf{die Kritik} — \textquotedblleft{}the criticism; the review\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Der neue Film hat gute Kritiken bekommen.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The new film got good reviews.}
\end{quote}

Plural: \emph{die Kritiken}. \emph{Kritik üben an} + dative — to criticize.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Kritik} was borrowed from French \emph{critique} (EtymDB), which goes back through Latin \emph{criticus} to Greek \emph{kritikós} \textquotedblleft{}able to judge\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{krínein} \textquotedblleft{}to judge\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
